title: Scramble for Africa (1881-1914)
key_facts: Period of rapid European colonization of African continent
Berlin Conference (1884-85) established rules for colonization
Africa divided among European powers with little regard for ethnic boundaries
By 1914, only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent
causes: Industrial Revolution's demand for raw materials and markets
European nationalism and competition for imperial prestige
Medical advances (quinine) enabling European survival in tropical regions
Military superiority with modern weapons against African resistance
outcome: European control over 90% of African territory
Exploitation of African resources and labor
Imposition of European borders and administrative systems
Legacy of political instability and ethnic conflicts

figures.name: Otto von Bismarck
figures.role: German chancellor who organized Berlin Conference

impacts: Created arbitrary national boundaries causing lasting conflicts
Economic exploitation and resource extraction patterns
Destruction of traditional African political systems
Foundation for later independence movements and decolonization
